Once these parallel activities are finished, the process splits again into two parallel paths. In one path, the parcels are loaded onto the truck, and then delivery instructions are sent to the transporter. In the other path, the order status is updated, followed by updating the stock levels.

Both parallel paths must complete—meaning the delivery instructions have been sent and the stock levels have been updated—before the process concludes.

Following the MRP execution, the capacity is evaluated to ensure that adequate resources are available to fulfill the production requirements. Based on this evaluation, the proposal is then scheduled and released.

After the proposal has been scheduled and released, the process order is confirmed. Subsequently, a transfer order or goods issue is created to move the required materials for production.

The goods issue is then confirmed to verify that the materials have been properly released. Once production is complete, the goods receipt is processed to record the finished products entering inventory.

Finally, the order settlement is performed to close out the process order and allocate all associated costs, bringing the process to its conclusion.

The process begins with searching for a customer. Once a customer is found, an offer is made to the customer.

After making the offer, the process checks whether an answer is received from the customer. If no answer is received, the process ends.

If an answer is received, an additional request is received from the customer, and details are provided in response.

Following the provision of details, the process determines whether the customer wants to proceed with a booking. If no booking is requested, the process ends.

If a booking is requested, a booking request is received, and the bill is sent to the customer.

The process then waits to receive payment from the customer. After receiving payment, one of two paths is taken: either the travel is booked and a booking confirmation is sent to the customer, or the customer is contacted. If the customer is contacted, the bill is sent again, and the payment cycle repeats until payment is successfully received.

Once the booking confirmation is sent after the travel is booked, the process ends.

Alternatively, if there are issues after receiving payment, the customer is contacted. After contacting the customer, the process loops back to sending the bill again, creating a cycle that continues until payment matters are resolved and the travel can be successfully booked.

Once all paths converge after either no answer, no booking decision, or successful booking confirmation, the process ends.

If the temperature is between 10 and 15 degrees, a standard notification is generated, and the process proceeds to send the generated messages before ending.

If the temperature falls outside this acceptable range, three parallel activities are initiated simultaneously: getting the container status, getting the client location, and getting the goods status.

For the container status branch, after retrieving the container status, the container status is estimated. If the status is acceptable, this branch proceeds to synchronize with the other parallel branches. If the status is not acceptable, a container change request is generated before continuing.

For the client location branch, after getting the client location, the distance is estimated. If the distance is 300 kilometers or more, this branch proceeds directly to synchronization. If the distance is less than 300 kilometers, the delivery time is estimated. If the delivery duration is acceptable, the branch continues to synchronization. If the duration is not acceptable, a route change request is generated before proceeding.

For the goods status branch, after getting the goods status, the goods status is estimated. A check is made to determine if there are any damages. If there are no damages, the branch proceeds to synchronization. If damages exist, they are evaluated to determine the damage level. If the goods are ruined, a removal request is generated. If the goods are compromised but not ruined, a price change request is generated. After either request is generated, the branch continues to synchronization.

Once all three parallel branches have completed and synchronized, the generated messages are sent, and the process ends.

If the temperature is between 10 and 15 degrees, a standard notification is generated, and the process proceeds to send the generated messages before ending.

If the temperature falls outside this acceptable range, three parallel activities are initiated simultaneously: getting the container status, getting the client location, and getting the goods status.

For the container path, after getting the container status, the container status is estimated. If the status is okay, this branch proceeds to synchronize with the other parallel branches. If the status is not okay, a container change request is generated before continuing.

For the client location path, after getting the client location, the distance is estimated. If the distance is 300 kilometers or more, this branch proceeds directly to synchronize with the other parallel branches. If the distance is less than 300 kilometers, the delivery time is estimated. If the delivery duration is okay, the branch continues to synchronization. If the duration is not okay, a route change request is generated before proceeding.

For the goods status path, after getting the goods status, the goods status is estimated. A check is then made to determine if there are any damages. If there are no damages, this branch proceeds to synchronize with the other parallel branches. If damages are present, the damages are evaluated. Based on the damage level, if the goods are ruined, a removal request is generated. If the goods are compromised, a price change request is generated. After generating either request, the branch continues to synchronization.

Once all three parallel branches have completed and synchronized, the process proceeds to send the generated messages and then ends.

0.text:
The process begins when consent to use personal data is required.

At this point, multiple activities are initiated simultaneously. The process adds information about profiling, including the logic involved, its significance, and the envisaged consequences of processing. Concurrently, the existence of several rights is documented: the right to access personal data, the right to rectify personal data, the right to erase personal data, the right to data portability, the right to withdraw consent, and the right to lodge a complaint to a supervisory authority.

In parallel, a check is performed to determine if the period for which personal data will be stored can be established. If the period can be determined, it is retrieved directly. If not, the criteria used to determine that period are retrieved instead. Either outcome then proceeds forward.

Simultaneously, a check is made to determine whether the data was obtained directly from the data subject. If the data was not obtained from the data subject, the source from which the personal data originated is retrieved. If it was obtained from the data subject, the process continues without this step.

Also running in parallel, a check determines whether personal data can be transferred internationally. If international transfer is not possible, information stating that personal data will be transferred internationally is added. Otherwise, the process proceeds directly.

Additionally, a check is performed to see if recipients of the data are present. If recipients are not present, they are retrieved. If recipients are already present, the process continues.

Furthermore, a check is made to determine if legitimate interests exist. If they do not, the legitimate interests are retrieved. If they do exist, the process moves forward.

Concurrently, the processing legal basis and processing purposes are retrieved. Identity and contact details are also retrieved, while separately, DPO details are requested. Once the DPO provides details, these are received, and this branch synchronizes with the identity retrieval.

Once all parallel activities have completed and synchronized, consent information is collected. Following this, consent is requested from the appropriate party. The response is then awaited—either consent is received, or a negation is received. Regardless of which response occurs, the process concludes and ends.

At this point, multiple activities are initiated simultaneously. Information is added regarding profiling about the logic involved, significance, and envisaged consequences of processing. Concurrently, a check is performed to determine whether the period for which personal data will be stored can be established. If the period can be determined, it is retrieved; if not, the criteria used to determine the period are retrieved instead. Both paths then converge before continuing.

At the same time, several rights-related notifications are added in parallel: the existence of the right to rectify personal data, the right to access personal data, the right to erase personal data, the right to data portability, the right to withdraw consent, and the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority.

Additionally, a check is made to determine whether the data was obtained directly from the data subject. If the data was not obtained from the data subject, the source from which the personal data originated is retrieved; otherwise, the process continues directly.

Simultaneously, a check is performed to see if personal data can be transferred internationally. If international transfer is not possible, information stating that personal data will be transferred internationally is added; otherwise, the process proceeds without this step.

A check is also made to determine whether recipients of the data are present. If recipients exist, they are retrieved; if not, the process continues. Similarly, legitimate interests are checked, and if present, they are retrieved.

In parallel, the processing legal basis and processing purposes are retrieved. Identity and contact details are also retrieved, while simultaneously DPO (Data Protection Officer) details are requested. Once the DPO details are received, this information joins the other retrieved identity and contact details.

Once all these parallel activities have completed and converged, consent information is collected. Following this, consent is formally requested.

After asking for consent, the response is awaited. Either consent is received or a negation (refusal) is received. Both outcomes lead to the conclusion of the process, which then ends.

9.text:
The process begins when consent to use personal data is required.

At this point, multiple activities are initiated simultaneously. These parallel activities include: adding information about profiling (including the logic involved, significance, and envisaged consequences of processing); checking if it is possible to determine the period for which personal data will be stored; adding the existence of various rights (the right to rectify personal data, the right to access personal data, the right to erase personal data, the right to data portability, the right to withdraw, and the right to lodge a complaint to a supervisory authority); checking if data has been obtained from the data subject; checking if personal data can be transferred internationally; checking if recipients are present; checking if legitimate interests are present; retrieving the processing legal basis; retrieving processing purposes; and retrieving identity and contact details along with asking the DPO (Data Protection Officer) for their details.

For the data storage period check, if it is possible to determine the period, then the period is retrieved. If not, the criteria used to determine the period are retrieved instead. Both paths then converge.

When checking if data was obtained from the data subject, if the answer is no, the source from which personal data originated is retrieved. If yes, or after retrieving the source, the process continues.

For international data transfer, if personal data cannot be transferred internationally, information stating that personal data will be transferred internationally is added. Both outcomes then merge.

Regarding recipients, if recipients are not present, they are retrieved. Similarly, for legitimate interests, if they are not present, they are retrieved. Both checks converge after completion.

Concurrently, identity and contact details are retrieved while DPO details are requested. Once DPO details are received, these parallel paths synchronize.

After all parallel branches complete, consent information is collected, followed by asking for consent. The response to the consent request leads to either receiving consent or receiving a negation. Both outcomes converge, and the process ends.
